stories.headline: MLB division series 2026: Live updates, analysis on Day 5
stories.summary: It's a loaded day in the 2026 MLB playoffs, with eight teams in action as both the ALDS and NLDS roll on.
stories.body:
We've got a Super Wednesday in the 2026 MLB playoffs. That's right, four games -- all win or go home for the teams with their backs against the wall. Does it get any better than that?

In the first American League game of the day, the Chicago White Sox hope to treat their home fans to a sweep of the Cleveland Guardians. Then it's Game 4 of the National League Division Series between the reigning back-to-back champion Los Angeles Dodgers and the Atlanta Braves, as the Braves fight to play another day. Next up, another Game 3: The Tampa Bay Rays, up 2-0, look to bounce the New York Yankees in the Bronx. Finally, the San Diego Padres hope to stave off elimination once again as they face the Milwaukee Brewers at Petco Park.

We'll have all the day's action covered -- from lineups and keys to the game before first pitch to in-game analysis and postgame takeaways.

Cleveland Guardians at Chicago White Sox (4 p.m.)
Starting pitchers: Daniel Espino vs. Sean Newcomb

What Guardians need to do to force Game 4: Score early and take some pressure off everyone starting with opener Daniel Espino. It's the formula that did not work at home in Game 2, but that doesn't mean it won't in a hostile environment in Game 3. By doing so, Cleveland can help quiet what should be a raucous crowd for the White Sox's first home playoff game in half a decade. Getting Jose Ramirez going would help, but he's not 100%, so Jo Adell, Steven Kwan, Chase DeLauter and Travis Bazzana need to pick up the slack. They've seen almost all of Chicago's pitchers. It's time to score some runs or go home for the winter. -- Jesse Rogers

Starting pitchers: Tyler Glasnow vs. Tyler Mahle

What Braves need to do to force Game 4: The task certainly got tougher after falling behind in the series with ace Chris Sale on the mound in Game 3, but there is still a path to getting this series back to L.A.

First, they need Mahle to keep doing what he has done since coming to Atlanta at the deadline. He posted at 1.99 ERA in nine regular-season starts and proved he can do it in the postseason last round against Philadelphia.

Secondly, the Braves must get Glasnow out of the game early like they did Blake Snell in Game 2. Glasnow made it through only five innings against the Braves in their regular-season matchup. The stakes are obviously higher this time, but that is exactly what Atlanta needs to do again as the Dodgers become much more vulnerable when the middle of their bullpen is in the game. -- Dan Mullen

What Yankees need to do to force Game 4: Score some runs early to ease the pressure. As ugly as the defense was in Game 2, the offense has been the bigger problem for New York in this series. Both Yankees runs this postseason came via home runs by the scalding Ben Rice. Their five hits are the fewest through two games of a playoff series in franchise history. The Yankees' three through five hitters -- Luis Garcia Jr., Spencer Jones and George Lombard Jr. -- went 0-for-21 with seven strikeouts and no walks at Tropicana Field. Manager Aaron Boone on Monday said he's considering making lineup changes against right-hander Nick Martinez after using the same lineup with eight left-handed hitters in the first two games. It wouldn't hurt. -- Jorge Castillo

He has been a godsend for a thin Padres rotation this season, and he is no stranger to big playoff moments from his time with the rival Los Angeles Dodgers. But his leash will be short.

The Padres also seem optimistic that Mason Miller will be back off the paternity list on Wednesday, and that Adrian Morejon will be recovered enough from a stiff shoulder to join him in the bullpen. If that ends up being the case, the Padres could be in good shape. If not, they'll have to get creative once more. -- Alden Gonzalez

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta signs new four-year Arsenal contract
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract to extend his stay at Arsenal, the Premier League champions confirmed.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract to extend his stay at Arsenal until 2030, the Premier League champions confirmed.

ESPN previously reported that Arteta was set to pen a new contract. His previous deal was due to expire at the end of this season.

The Spaniard led Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 23 years last season and also won the FA Cup in 2020.

"It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," he said in a statement.

"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.

"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together."

He joined the club in December 2019 after serving as assistant manager at Manchester City, and is currently the longest-serving head coach in the Premier League.

Co-chairs Stan and Josh Kroenke said: "It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead in this special relationship. Last season was an incredible moment in Arsenal's history, a moment in which we created memories that will last a lifetime. We're determined to create many more in the years ahead.

"We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019."

Arsenal have also confirmed that Arteta's coaching staff have also renewed their deals for four more years.

stories.headline: Are Texans and Chargers this bad? And how do we bet the Rams one month in?
stories.summary: Four weeks into the NFL season, what do we know, and what can we expect moving forward?
stories.body:
Four weeks into the NFL season, the Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers are winless, a deeper stumble than anticipated. Which team can rebound, and which problems are real? The San Francisco 49ers look strong, as predicted, but is that start sustainable? Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Rams are Super Bowl favorites, yet their regular-season win total still offers a fade.

The Texans aren't this bad, the preseason thesis just cracked
Texans: 0-4, 0-4 ATS (45-1 to win Super Bowl, 18-1 entering Week 1)

The biggest preseason concern for Houston was whether the offense could finally complement an elite defense. Instead, the defense has become part of the problem. Houston is allowing 27 points per game after allowing 17 PPG last season. More concerning, the offseason investment in the run game hasn't translated. David Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry, leaving C.J. Stroud responsible for creating most of the offense (again).

Stroud has actually been solid, throwing for 1,141 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions. It's the lack of red zone execution -- top half of the league in attempts, bottom 10 in touchdowns scored. There's reason to expect improvement: Houston has essentially matched its opponents in total yardage, owns a positive turnover margin and has lost two games by four points or less. This looks more like an underperforming team than a terrible one.

The fix starts with the run game, even if that means leaning more on Woody Marks or adjusting the blocking approach rather than forcing Montgomery into something that isn't working. Defensively, Houston has to limit explosive passes; the pass rush is still getting home, so the secondary needs to capitalize on that pressure.

There's room for regression toward competence, but it shouldn't involve Stroud becoming Superman -- just play complementary football. Houston's season win total was 9.5 going into the season. At 0-4, the market has dropped them to 7.5. Seven wins is the new benchmark.

The Chargers lost their foundation before it ever had an identity
Chargers: 0-4, 0-3-1 ATS (100-1 to win Super Bowl, 17-1 entering Week 1)

The Chargers were a preseason regression candidate because last year's 11 wins were helped by a soft schedule and close-game success. The bad news: their 0-4 start goes beyond regression.

The offense Mike McDaniel was supposed to unlock has been undermined by the exact concern identified preseason: offensive line health. OT Rashawn Slater is doubtful, OT Joe Alt and G Trevor Penning are questionable, and C Tyler Biadasz is on injured reserve. Justin Herbert is pressing behind unstable protection, turning the ball over and failing to create explosive plays.

The defense has declined without coordinator Jesse Minter, though it has created opportunities, forcing five turnovers against Buffalo -- yet losing the game anyway. The fix is simplification: lean on Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, use motion and quicker throws, and stop asking Herbert to rescue every possession.

The Chargers are probably better than 0-4, but the schedule still limits their recovery. Under 5.5 wins at +118 is worth a look, and I would keep fading them as favorites until this offense proves itself.

Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures.

The 49ers' season win total is ahead of schedule, the championship case remains untested

San Francisco's 4-0 start has validated my preseason OVER 9.5 prediction. I'm still not quite ready to validate the 49ers as a Super Bowl team, not at the +850 price. Kyle Shanahan has kept the offense efficient despite injuries, and Brock Purdy has been outstanding. The receiving additions are producing, the run game has multiple answers, and San Francisco is winning without relying heavily on turnovers or unusual kicking luck.

Still, context matters. The opener against the Rams was played abroad, Miami might be the NFL's worst team, Arizona is rebuilding, and Denver has a strong defense without a punishing offense. The 49ers handled that stretch as a good team should. My problem with the hype is that the opening schedule hasn't forced the Niners to show that their limited pass rush and vulnerable secondary can survive against elite quarterbacks.

Their Super Bowl price has shortened from 14-1 to +850. That move is a reflection of the current record more than actual substantial proof. If you have a preseason ticket, great. I wouldn't buy +850 now.

NFL futures prediction: Rams UNDER 10.5 wins (+116)

The Rams being Super Bowl favorites and going under 10.5 wins can both make sense. The Super Bowl market is pricing their ceiling, with Sean McVay, a healthy Matthew Stafford and a roster capable of beating anyone in January.

The win total is about surviving 13 more regular-season games with almost zero wiggle room. The Rams are 2-2, so the over requires a 9-4 finish. That's a demanding pace for a team facing a difficult schedule, with Stafford showing turnover volatility and Myles Garrett on injured reserve.

The number has dropped from 11.5 preseason to 10.5, so protection with the 11-win middle is lost. Still, the +116 keeps the under playable. The Rams can still be one of the NFL's best teams, reach the playoffs and even win the Super Bowl while finishing 10-7. We know what the ceiling for the Rams can be. This wager is betting against regular-season perfection.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 40
Goals: 36
Assists: 17

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami

Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Mercedes confirm George Russell engine penalty at Singapore Grand Prix
stories.summary: Mercedes has confirmed that George Russell will serve an engine penalty at the Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday.
stories.body:
Mercedes has confirmed George Russell will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to an engine penalty.

Russell retired from third at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia due to a power unit failure with six laps remaining.

Mercedes need to introduce replacement power unit to Russell's car in Singapore, which will take him above his quota of power unit components for the season and result in a back-of-the-grid penalty.

It is another setback to his championship hopes. His teammate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the F1 standings sits at 84 points, and Russell is second.

Team principal Toto Wolff's pre-race statement said: "George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty [in Singapore], which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia.

"That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for. Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport and our focus now is on giving him the best possible car and opportunities to fight back through the field."

After reliability issues earlier this year, Mercedes was already planning for Russell to take an additional power unit and the resulting penalty before the end of the season, but was not expecting to do so in Singapore where overtaking in the race is notoriously difficult.

The failure in Malaysia forced the team's hand as Russell does not have enough low-mileage components in his pool of engine parts to avoid taking a new power unit this weekend.

The situation is further complicated for Russell as Mercedes was planning to bring a performance upgrade to its power unit at the U.S. Grand Prix in two weeks' time, which the team had hoped would coincide with the introduction of Russell's final power unit of the year.

Mercedes has not yet confirmed whether the upgrade can be fast-tracked for introduction in Singapore or whether Russell will need to use older specification parts this weekend.

Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord warned in Malaysia that Russell may face a "double whammy" if he then has to take another penalty at the U.S. Grand Prix to access the upgraded power unit for the rest of the season.

Wolff also confirmed that his team will use this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix to assess the aerodynamic upgrades it brought to its car in Malaysia.

Despite expectations that the update would move the championship leaders comfortably ahead of its competitors, Max Verstappen's Red Bull proved to be fastest car at Sepang while Mercedes was left scratching its head over its relative lack of performance.

Wolff revealed his team would use the Singapore weekend to run direct comparisons between its previous aerodynamic package and the new updates.

"Malaysia was obviously a very difficult weekend for us," Wolff said. "We have spent the days since then working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been.

"We have identified several areas we need to investigate further, but F1 doesn't offer simple answers and we need more evidence before drawing firm conclusions.

"Singapore gives us an immediate opportunity to continue that work. The characteristics of the circuit are very different and that will help us build a clearer picture of where we are.

"That is why we will evaluate both the latest update package and our previous specification across the weekend to ensure we fully understand the direction we need to take."

stories.headline: Nigerian connection runs through Mystics rise as Kiki Iriafen breaks out in playoff run
stories.summary: Fresh from helping team USA win the World Cup last month, Kiki Iriafen's second WNBA season ended with a first round elimination to the Atlanta Dream.
stories.body:
Fresh from helping the United States win the World Cup last month, Kiki Iriafen's second WNBA season ended with a first round elimination to the Atlanta Dream, but finishing the game with yet another double-double was an indication of just how quickly the Nigerian-American forward has grown into a central piece of the Washington Mystics' present.

Iriafen helped herself to 15 points and 16 rebounds in Washington's 93-75 loss to the Atlanta Dream, completing her first postseason with double-doubles in both games of the first-round series for an average of 15 points and 15 rebounds in the playoffs after a regular season in which she emerged as Washington's leading rebounder and one of their top three scorers.

Alongside her for much of that run was Michaela Onyenwere - another Nigerian-American forward whose contribution came from a different place. The 2021 WNBA Rookie of the Year came to Washington with five seasons of league experience to help the youngest roster in the WNBA and became enough of a veteran voice that her teammates began calling her "Coach Mic."

And just like she did on her Draft night when strutting it out in a dress that reflected her Nigerian heritage, Iriafen says she is driven by the Nigerian spirit

"My Nigerian heritage has been something that I've always wanted to promote," she said. "Michaela and I were just talking about what should we do. Like, we should go celebrate. But it's super special. My Nigerian heritage has been something that I've always wanted to promote. I am Nigerian American, but I feel like both sides of me are equally as important to me."

Together, both have given Washington the Nigerian connection within a team that improved from 16 wins in 2025 to a franchise-record 28 this season and returned to the playoffs for the first time since 2023.

Iriafen's rise, to go with the likes of USA teammate Sonia Citron, and Shakira Austin, was at the heart of that improvement.

After averaging 13.3 points and 8.5 rebounds as a rookie, the 23-year-old increased those numbers to 15.3 points and 9.5 rebounds this season while shooting better than 50% from the field. She finished behind Austin and Citron in scoring and led the Mystics in rebounding, narrowly ahead of Austin.

She also recorded a Mystics single-season record 23 double-doubles, and earned a second consecutive All-Star selection - numbers that helped get her onto Team USA's World Cup roster.

The postseason provided another test - one that Iriafen confronted head on, even if it was her first experience.

Foul trouble in Game 1 meant she played only 23 minutes against Atlanta, but still finished with 15 points and 14 rebounds. Nine of those rebounds came on the offensive end, tying a Washington franchise record for offensive rebounds in a game and helping the Mystics outrebound the Dream 50-31.

"I really felt like I wasn't able to help my team in the first half, so I wanted to do that for my teammates," Iriafen said.

Game 2 was much better, as she stayed on the floor for more than 35 minutes. Her 30 rebounds over the two games were the second-most by a player through her first two WNBA playoff games.

The numbers continued a progression that began almost immediately after Washington selected her with the No. 4 pick in the 2025 draft. Initially, the Mystics leaned heavily on Iriafen's rebounding, transition running and ability to finish around the basket. Now, her offensive responsibilities have gradually expanded to include more post touches, screening actions and opportunities to make decisions with the ball.

Her development has also come alongside Citron - Washington's other cornerstone from the 2025 draft. Citron led the Mystics in playoff scoring with 25 points in each game against Atlanta, while Iriafen controlled the glass.

The partnership leaves Washington with two young players who have already translated regular-season production into the postseason - one that coach Sydney Johnson was pleased with as he singled both out for praise.

"I'm sitting beside two players who played their first playoff games, and there was a lot of good stuff out there," he said. "I'm immensely disappointed for the result, but I also think what this group has accomplished and how the DC community has rallied around this group has been amazing. They've written history. I am excited to take this first step forward with Kiki and Sonia and our whole group."

For Iriafen, that development has unfolded alongside an identity she has repeatedly said matters a lot to her.

"Being Nigerian is huge for me," Iriafen told House of Victory earlier this year. "It's my culture, it's a big part of who I am.

"There are so many young Nigerian hoopers and young Nigerians that I'm an inspiration to and I just want to showcase that being Nigerian is cool."

That connection was there well before she played her first WNBA game. Who can forget Kiki owning the show at the 2025 WNBA draft in a custom dress designed by Nigerian designer Nneka Alexander, while accompanied by members of her family equally attired in traditional Nigerian clothing?

"My parents always say Naija no dey carry last," she said. "So I feel like in everything that I do, I try to strive for that. So that's kind of the motto of my life.

"Something in Nigeria is the resources aren't always as equal, but just understanding that it doesn't matter how you get there, there's still an opportunity. There's still a way. So I just really want to carry myself with class and really truly be a great role model."

The draft took her to Washington, which offered an even bigger connection to Nigeria, with its huge Nigerian population.

A year later, the Mystics added Onyenwere, whose route to the capital was considerably longer. Selected sixth overall by New York in 2021, Onyenwere won WNBA Rookie of the Year before stops with Phoenix and Chicago. Washington signed her to a multiyear deal this year and immediately installed her in a starting lineup filled with younger players.

Onyenwere, 26 years old when the season began, was the oldest player on the roster.

"We call her 'Coach Mic.' She knows what she's talking about," Iriafen said. "She's a great leader, great teammate and great person."

The connection between them predates the Mystics. They first crossed paths when Iriafen was a high school prospect considering UCLA and Onyenwere was playing for the Bruins.

Their Nigerian heritage provided another common thread. Onyenwere's father Peter competed for Nigeria in track and field, and her grandmother became one of the memorable images of the 2021 WNBA draft when she danced in traditional Nigerian clothing behind Onyenwere during a television interview when her name was called.

"I am just so proud to be Nigerian, and I never let anyone forget it," Onyenwere said. "I make sure I let people know I am Nigerian because it is a big part of who I am.

"From Draft Night, I was getting messages from young Nigerian kids who are in Nigeria, saying you are an inspiration. You don't really think those things until you see those messages. Like, I am influencing people in a different continent."

Both women have also represented the United States internationally - a clear sign of the dual identity they have carried and basked in through their basketball careers. Iriafen helped the United States win the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, appearing in four games during the Americans' unbeaten run to the title.

Onyenwere represented USA Basketball in both 3x3 and 5-on-5 competition in 2019. She played on the American 3x3 circuit and later helped the United States win silver at the Pan American Games.

Nigeria did attempt to bring Onyenwere into the D'Tigress program for the 2024 Paris Olympics, but she was unable to join the team after failing to receive clearance in time.

In adding to the Nigerian connection, her role in Washington this season has been more about helping to provide stability around a young core.

Onyenwere averaged 9.0 points during the regular season while starting alongside Iriafen, Austin and Citron. She scored eight points in the opening playoff loss to Atlanta before adding 12 in Game 2.

Washington's season ended there, but Iriafen's first experience of playoff basketball provided another marker in a second season in which her responsibilities and production grew and both playoff games provided a clear measure of how far her role has expanded and where Washington could take it next.

She finished the two-game series averaging 15 points and 15 rebounds, with 13 offensive rebounds, after leading Washington in rebounding during the regular season and establishing career highs in both scoring and rebounding.

"This whole season has just been just a learning process for me," Iriafen said after Game 2. "It was nothing like my first season.

"I feel like just even during my undergrad, doing tough majors and still being a professional athlete, just showcasing that, whatever you put your mind to that you can do it."

For the Mystics, the next part of that learning process will be figuring out how much more Iriafen can handle. They already have one of the league's most productive young rebounders and an increasingly reliable interior scorer. Her three assists in Game 2 also offered a glimpse of how her role could expand as a passer and decision-maker.

Onyenwere, meanwhile, provided an experienced voice alongside her during that development, four years after becoming WNBA Rookie of the Year herself, giving the Mystics a Nigerian-American one-two punch.

The season may have ended earlier than they or the Mystics wanted, but it also provided a silver lining, with Washington back in the playoffs and Iriafen having experienced the stage that she wanted, even if she failed to conquer it. For now.

"Playoffs are the biggest stage," Iriafen said after Game 1. "This is the stage we want to be on."

On the evidence of this run, it is one that she will be returning to for the foreseeable future. And she will continue to be driven by that Naija no dey carry last spirit.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Matchmaking, inactivity -- and, yes, fights -- shift MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
The fighter who won a UFC championship on Saturday does not move an inch in the ESPN divisional rankings. But several other fighters who did not even compete over the weekend do rise in their divisions' top 10s. One shifts from the top of one division's rankings to the middle of the pack in another weight class.

The new champion is Natalia Silva, who cruised past unranked Wang Cong at UFC 332 to capture the vacant women's flyweight title. Silva stays put at No. 2, however, below Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the title while recovering from injury.

Several other weight classes saw significant shifts, in some cases because of a lack of fights and in one case because of a fight booking for the future.

The most significant move is Alex Pereira shifting into the heavyweight rankings following the UFC's announcement that he will face Sergei Pavlovich on Dec. 12. It will be the second straight heavyweight fight for the former middleweight and light heavyweight champion, who has been No. 1 in the 205-pound rankings. He now moves to the heavyweight top 10, where he is ranked No. 7, two spots behind Pavlovich.

At light heavyweight, everyone previously below Pereira moves up, with ex-champion Magomed Ankalaev now No. 1. New to the top 10 are ninth-ranked Bogdan Guskov and No. 10 Robert Whittaker, as Khalil Rountree Jr. is out because he has not fought in over a year.

Also ineligible because of inactivity is middleweight Nassourdine Imavov, who is replaced in the 185-pound rankings by Christian Leroy Duncan. Perfect timing, as Duncan fights No. 5 Brendan Allen on Saturday's UFC card.

The other top-10 newcomer is men's bantamweight Payton Talbott, who knocked out Deiveson Figueiredo at UFC 332 to oust him from the rankings.

stories.headline: 'One of the greats': Roosters' Daniel Tupou retires
stories.summary: The Sydney Roosters will be without dependable winger Daniel Tupou next season, after he confirmed he will retire with immediate effect.
stories.body:
Trent Robinson says Daniel Tupou will be remembered as one of the Sydney Roosters' all-time greats, after the four-time premiership-winning winger announced his retirement from the NRL.

Tupou is ending his 15-year career on a high after helping the Roosters win Sunday's Grand Final against Newcastle.

The 35-year-old, who had been coy about his future all season, became just the sixth player in Roosters history to win four premierships with the club.

Across a 307-game, one-club career, the winger scored 198 tries, the third most of any player in premiership history behind Ken Irvine and Alex Johnston.

"When you look at what Daniel Tupou has achieved over 15 seasons, he will stand as one of the greats," Robinson said in a statement.

"But those numbers only tell part of the story of Toops and what he means to this club.

"Since he made his debut, he has represented what we want a Rooster to be.

"He has been incredibly consistent, selfless and dependable, and whenever there has been a big moment or a tough moment, he has been present.

"Toops revolutionised the aerial game at the Sydney Roosters and became the greatest high-ball specialist of all time."

Tupou's exit comes as the Roosters prepare for a big off-season exodus over the coming weeks.

Fellow winger Mark Nawaqanitawase and back-rower Angus Crichton are moving to rugby union, Daly Cherry-Evans is heading to Super League side Hull FC, and Connor Watson is joining St George Illawarra.

But none of them get close to having the impact the towering winger has had on the Roosters since his NRL debut in 2012.

As well as four premierships (2013, 2018, 2019, 2026), Tupou has won three World Club Challenges and played Test matches for both Tonga and Australia.

He was part of the Tongan side that defeated the Kangaroos in 2019, in one of the biggest upsets in international rugby league history.

Tupou played 10 times for NSW at State of Origin level between 2014 and 2022.

"We love Toops, we're incredibly proud of him, and his name will always hold a very special place in the history of the Sydney Roosters," Robinson said.

Tupou retires as the greatest try-scorer in Roosters history after surpassing Anthony Minichiello in 2023.

He has the second-most appearances for Easts, behind prop Jared Waerea-Hargreabes.

"To have played my whole NRL career at one club means a lot to me," Tupou said.

"The Roosters gave me my opportunity and this has become my home.

"To play more than 300 games, win four premierships and share those moments with so many great teammates is something I'll always be proud of."

NSW State of Origin games/tries: 10/3

Tonga games/tries: 23/13
