stories.headline: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero
stories.summary: The Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its core, wouldn't have been possible without Football Leaks and its founder, Rui Pinto. However, he is a complicated figure, with light and dark to his actions.
stories.body:
It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

Had he not obtained and shared more than 70 million documents with the German magazine Der Spiegel starting in 2016, culminating in the publication of their massive "Football Leaks" investigation two years later, there would have been no investigation of City -- not by UEFA, not by the Premier League, not by any of the other bodies that may get involved once the current process is concluded.

Simply put, there would have been no legal basis for anyone to do this. We would have had an alternate reading of history -- one where City get new owners, Abu Dhabi United Group in 2009, spend a ton of money, watch their revenues skyrocket and dominate the game, all the while complying with every single financial regulation set before them. (The only exception was in 2014, when they breached UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations and eventually signed a three-year settlement agreement.)

Whatever the ultimate outcome of the City case -- whether it results in expulsion from the Premier League and Sheikh Mansour having to shell out hundreds of millions in fines and compensation, or somehow ends in the club getting most, if not all, of the charges overturned on appeal -- this should be a massive wake-up call to those running the game. The message: football needs better oversight and more transparency.

Whichever way the dust settles, this much is obvious: the system failed. Either City did participate in a massive "sham" (to quote from the verdict), effectively cheating while the system failed to notice and act, or the Premier League is so inept that it has somehow been duped by a conspiracy of legacy clubs into conducting an ultimately futile eight-year investigation. Neither outcome is good; in fact, both are embarrassingly bad for the world's most successful league.

What would better oversight and transparency look like? How about something like we have in the NFL, where information about salaries, sponsorships and other revenue is shared not just with the league, but with teams around the league itself as well as the players' union. That creates a virtuous cycle of self-policing and makes it much harder to engage in financial skullduggery. (Harder, but not impossible, as old-school San Francisco 49ers fans will confirm.)

In the Premier League, far too much is a closely guarded secret in the name of "competitive advantage" -- clubs, not just City, disclose as little as legally allowed as if they were running some normal business, not a hugely important public trust like the world's most popular sport.

All of which brings us back to Pinto.

Is it fair to call him some sort of hero, saving football from itself? He would say so; in fact, he testified in court that he views himself as a whistleblower, exposing corruption in football. On his original Football Leaks site, he wrote that "the sport we love so much is rotten and it is time to say enough." Except his approach to the task was distinctly scattershot, simply dumping tens of millions of documents online.

Some of these documents suggested nefarious intent and led to investigations and prosecutions. (It wasn't just about Man City, but illegal third-party ownership schemes involving a company called Doyen Sports, as well as alleged tax evasion involving Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Jose Mourinho, Luka Modric and others.)

There were documents containing nuggets of information that were interesting and possibly newsworthy, like the fact that the European Super League plot went as far back as 2016 or that Paris Saint-Germain used ethnic origin criteria when scouting players. Others still were, at best, football oddities, like the report that Liverpool put a £1 million bonus in Mario Balotelli's contract if he got sent off less than three times in a season.

Or that Ronaldo's staff (including housekeepers, chefs and drivers) had to sign a nondisclosure agreement that stopped them from revealing anything about his private life until 70 years after his death. Or that Ronaldo got paid €1.1 million by a Saudi communications company in exchange for a four-hour photo shoot, five signed shirts and two social media posts. Or that Real Madrid purposefully misrepresented the Gareth Bale fee allegedly so that Ronaldo, whose transfer fee was marginally lower, would continue to believe that he was the most expensive player of all time.

The vast majority of leaked documents were frightfully boring and of zero news value. I remember spending several hours of my life -- time I'll never get back -- reading the contract of left-back Rayan Aït-Nouri when he moved to Angers as a youth team player, a document Pinto had posted on his original Football Leaks site prior to his collaboration with Der Spiegel. There was nothing there other than the invasion of a teenage kid's privacy.

Two other factors cast shade on Pinto's work. One is his attempted extortion of Doyen Sports in 2015 -- a Lisbon court found him guilty in 2023 and handed a four-year suspended sentence -- when he contacted their CEO, Nelio Lucas, and demanded half a million Euros to keep hacked documents private. Pinto has always claimed innocence, saying he was simply trying to "verify" the documents; the court ruled otherwise.

The other is that it's still not entirely clear how he obtained the documents, whether he did it on someone's behalf or whether he was acting alone. His story has evolved over the years, originally claiming he was given the documents, then admitting he had hacked some of the victims. Here, it gets even more murky. Doyen Sports were clearly hacked; probably City too. But the sheer scale and variety of the documents suggests that, in some cases, either Pinto is some sort of genius hacker or he wasn't acting alone.

It's worth noting Pinto has also suffered as a result of his actions. He spent years hiding in Hungary, from where he was extradited to Portugal in 2019. He has made enemies around the globe. He now has a criminal record, and he says he has received multiple death threats, a claim credible enough that the Portuguese government placed him under witness protection in 2020, though his lawyers claim that those protections would cease next Saturday, Oct. 10. Pinto posted on his social media channels last Friday that he was crowdfunding to handle his security costs.

If there is some good to come out of this whole tale, it's not just that tax evaders and bad actors (if the appeals process holds up the independent panel's verdict) are brought to justice. It's that this is an opportunity for the game to regulate itself better and for tax authorities to do a better job. There's light and dark in Rui Pinto's actions, and we may never know which side was stronger in motivating him. But without him, there would be no light at the end of the tunnel and for that, we ought to be grateful.

stories.headline: Early 2026 NFL trends for the 49ers, Vikings, Bucs, Texans, Giants, Browns
stories.summary: Just how good are the 49ers? Are the Texans and Bucs better than their records? Are the Giants and Browns worse? We put the NFL season's first month in historical context.
stories.body:
Early in every NFL season, you hear a lot about the pace of certain stats. But most of the time when you see that a player or team is on pace to record a certain stat, you have no idea about issues for similar things in the past.

Performance is usually going to regress toward the mean. Teams and players that started superhot will cool. Teams and players that were terrible early will get better. So we don't want to compare a team's performance after four games to what other teams have done over 16- and 17-game seasons. We want to compare that performance to what others have done in the same number of games.

We can do that with DVOA (defense-adjusted value over average) stats. We've gone back and rerun every season since 1977 to see what DVOA would have looked like as of Week 4. Here, teams are rated solely based on what they did through four games (and what opponents did over that time). And every year of DVOA is normalized so that we're comparing teams to the averages of their own era, not to what teams do in today's game.

This year, there's one team in particular playing at a historical level. You might not realize quite how good the San Francisco 49ers have been. But will their usual spate of injuries prevent them from living up to their September greatness with the franchise's sixth Super Bowl title? Let's look closer and explore three other early trends that I've noticed in the DVOA data.

1. The 49ers are the 11th-best team overall through four games since 1977 (and have the third-best passing offense)
The 49ers shocked everyone when they not only beat the favored Rams in Week 1 but destroyed them. We've sort of written off that Rams performance because of the whole jetlag issue, but maybe a part of the 49ers winning was being really good?

San Francisco has continued to win games, mostly decisively. It dominated the Dolphins in Week 2 and had a big fourth quarter to beat the Broncos in Week 4. The Niners' Week 3 victory over Arizona was 36-30, but a play-by-play breakdown suggests the 49ers outplayed the Cardinals by a much wider margin. They outgained the Cards 8.7 yards to 4.5 yards per play but had 31 fewer plays. The efficiency predicts future performance better than the raw number of plays.

Put it all together, and the 49ers are No. 1 in my DVOA ratings with a historically high number. Only 10 teams since 1977 have been higher through the first four games.

The 49ers' success is primarily being driven by their superb passing game, with quarterback Brock Purdy leading the league in QBR. Sure, the 49ers rank fifth in defensive DVOA and ninth in run offense, but the passing game is historically good. Since 1977, the only teams with a better passing game through four games were the 1998 Broncos with John Elway and a shockingly strong 1999 Washington team with Brad Johnson at quarterback. Yes, Washington in 1999 scored 37.5 points per game over the first four weeks, while Johnson averaged 298 passing yards and 9.8 yards per attempt, nine touchdowns and zero interceptions.

That puts the current 49ers slightly ahead of some all-time great passing clubs, including the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams, the 2013 Broncos with Peyton Manning and the 1984 Dolphins with Dan Marino.

What we can expect: Our first table shows that not every team that starts this hot is guaranteed to win the Super Bowl, but there are also some all-time great squads on that list. If we expanded it to 20 teams, we would add five more Super Bowl champions: 1977 Cowboys, 1985 Bears, 1990 Giants, 1998 Broncos and 2009 Saints. Overall, the previous 20 best teams by DVOA through four games won nine Super Bowls and lost three.

The problem for the 49ers, of course, is the injury bug. San Francisco has been among the most injured teams in the league nearly every season since coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch took over. Already this season, they've been without top edge rusher Nick Bosa (calf) and starting defensive tackle Alfred Collins (knee). Four different wide receivers are on injured reserve, and veteran Mike Evans was limited in last week's practices with a rib injury. In fact, the 49ers are running out of space on their injured reserve list.

It will be tough for the 49ers to maintain this type of all-time great performance as starters give way to backups ... who in turn give way to third-stringers.

2. The Vikings are the eighth-worst 4-0 team since 2000
Everyone saw the 49ers dominate the Rams on national television, so their 4-0 start isn't such a surprise. Kansas City is also 4-0, and most observers expected a rebound from last year's down season.

The Vikings (4-0) are the third undefeated team, but their record is perhaps a little more surprising. They can barely get any offense going. Three of their four wins came by a touchdown or less. And this week, they barely beat a Miami team that is widely considered the worst in the league.

The offense-defense split for the Vikings is remarkable. They currently rank 31st in offensive DVOA, ahead of only the Chargers. They're second in defensive DVOA, barely behind only the Seahawks. And the Vikings have the benefit of this season's best special teams unit, with Myles Price leading the league in kick and punt return yardage.

Add it all together and the Vikings are 10th in total DVOA despite going undefeated. (They're even worse in ESPN's Football Power Index, ranking 14th.) That makes them the eighth-worst 4-0 team by DVOA since 2000. If we go back to 1977, the Vikings are still 13th worst out of 136 teams to start 4-0.

What we can expect: The bad news for the Vikings is that offense, in general, is more stable and predictive than defense or special teams. That means it is more likely that the Vikings offense will continue to struggle than it is that the defense and special teams will continue to be outstanding.

The good news is that plenty of teams have ridden a suspect 4-0 start all the way to the Super Bowl. It's good to bank those four wins, no matter how well you play, and a number of teams on our list improved over the course of the season. Out of the dozen worst 4-0 teams since 2000, five made the Super Bowl and two won the Lombardi Trophy.

The fact that the Vikings could go either way is emphasized by the two most similar teams on our list. The 2015 Broncos ranked first on defense and 30th on offense after four weeks. Peyton Manning never got his groove back, but the defense didn't regress and led the Broncos to a Super Bowl title. On the other hand, the Vikings are also similar to the 2012 Cardinals, who ranked 28th on offense and fifth on defense after four weeks. That team completely collapsed, constantly shuffling through backup quarterbacks after an injury to starter Kevin Kolb.

3. The Texans and Buccaneers rank among the best 0-4 teams since 1977
The Texans were a popular Super Bowl pick out of the AFC before the season began. They are supposed to have one of the best defenses in the league and were hoping the offense would improve. Instead, the Texans have lost their first four games, three of them at home. Their season seems over.

The same appears to be true for the Buccaneers. They weren't quite as popular as the Texans in the preseason, but plenty of observers believed they could return to the top of the NFC South. They've also started 0-4 and lost three games at home.

What if I told you that the Texans and Buccaneers have actually been close to NFL average when you break down the play-by-play and look at their efficiency? Houston ranks 17th in the league and Tampa Bay ranks 18th. There are 150 teams since 1977 that have started the season either 0-4 or 0-3-1, and out of all of them, Houston and Tampa Bay rank third and fourth in DVOA.

Houston's offense has been a lot better than you think, an unexpected 13th in DVOA this season. It's the defense that has disappointed, ranking only 15th. Meanwhile, in Tampa Bay, the young defense that some folks believed could be pretty good has, in fact, been pretty good. It ranks ninth in DVOA. But the offense looks rough, ranking 24th. Quarterback Baker Mayfield played poorly for three weeks and is now sidelined by a dislocated thumb.

Houston has been outscored by 25 points overall, but it has allowed the exact number of yards as it has gained (1,375), with the same yards per play average and a positive turnover differential. (Quarterback C.J. Stroud hasn't thrown an interception yet.) The Buccaneers have been outgained by 18 yards, although they have a minus-5 turnover differential. All four of their losses have come by a touchdown or less.

What we can expect: Only one of the other top 0-4 teams turned things around enough to finish with a winning record. The 2004 Bills finished the season with the highest DVOA of any team that has ever missed the playoffs. They fell short when they lost to the Pittsburgh backups in Week 17. But they went 9-3 over the 12 games after their 0-4 start. Other teams on the list, such as the 2011 Vikings and 1980 Jets, played down to their records for the rest of the season.

The only team to turn around a 0-4 season and make the playoffs was the 1992 Chargers. That team was not one of the best 0-4 teams by DVOA. They were legitimately bad at the start, ranking 24th out of 28 teams in DVOA, before going 11-1 for the rest of the season. Now we have 17 games in a season instead of 16, and seven playoff teams per conference instead of six, which makes it a little easier for the Texans or Buccaneers.

ESPN's FPI projections still give the Texans a 16% chance of making the playoffs. The division title will be tough with Jacksonville playing so well, but the wild-card round is a realistic goal. The FPI simulation has the Buccaneers at only 5% odds, although the NFC South might be an easier division to win. FPI has Tampa Bay much lower than DVOA, in part because it's accounting for a few more weeks with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback instead of Mayfield.

4. The Giants and Browns rank among the worst 3-1 teams since 2000
When the Browns got crushed 34-10 in Jacksonville in Week 1, it seemed like they were going to be the same old Browns. So it's extremely surprising that Cleveland has pulled off three one-score wins since then. The Browns have finally given life to fans who have dealt with years at the bottom of the AFC standings.

Some people thought the Giants could be this year's breakthrough turnaround team, and they beat the Cowboys 28-20 in Week 1. After a Week 2 loss to the Rams, they went on to win their next two games over Tennessee and Arizona despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the regular season (knee).

DVOA is not impressed. The Browns rank 23rd and the Giants are 22nd. FPI is even less impressed, with the Browns 26th and the Giants 31st. A part of the issue is that advanced stats look at every play of the season. Terrible performance in the big losses (Browns to Jaguars, Giants to Rams) overwhelms play in the three close wins for each team.

The Browns and Giants do not rank among the 10 worst 3-1 teams by DVOA since 1977, but they do rank among the worst 3-1 teams since the turn of the century.

What we can expect: The 2016 Rams collapsed from a 3-1 start to finish 4-12. But of the bad 3-1 teams, a few of them have made the playoffs, and the 2010 Bears even made it to the NFC Championship Game -- in part because they got to face a worse team, the 7-9 NFC West champion Seahawks, in the divisional round.

I think it's more likely that the Browns and Giants will play down to their DVOA over the rest of the season rather than playing better and continuing to win games. ESPN's FPI agrees. It gives the Browns an 18% chance of making the postseason, while the Giants have just a 4% chance. FPI puts a lot of weight on the quarterback's performance, and while Deshaun Watson is a surprising 18th with a 58.4 QBR, Jameis Winston is down at 28th with a 33.3 QBR.

stories.headline: Fire beat Whitecaps in matchup of ex-Bayern teammates Lewandowski, Müller
stories.summary: Philip Zinckernagel scored early in the second half and Maren Haile-Selassie had a late goal and an assist as Chicago Fire FC beat the Vancouver Whitecaps 3-1 on Tuesday night.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- Philip Zinckernagel scored early in the second half, Maren Haile-Selassie had a late goal and an assist as Chicago Fire FC beat the Vancouver Whitecaps 3-1 on Tuesday night in a matchup of former Bayern Munich teammates Robert Lewandowski and Thomas Müller.

Lewandowski and Muller spent eight seasons together at Bayern from 2014-22. The stars were supposed to reunite in MLS months ago before wildfires postponed the highly anticipated matchup.

Lewandowski's unselfish pass to a wide-open Haile-Selassie at the back post capped the scoring in the 88th minute. Lewandowski, who returned to Chicago early from international duty with Poland after a yellow-card suspension ruled him out of Monday's match, has six goals and three assists through his first 12 MLS appearances.

Chicago (13-8-6) moved past Charlotte into fourth place in the Eastern Conference standings. The top four finishers earn home-field advantage in the first round of the playoffs.

Vancouver (15-7-5) remains atop the Western Conference with 50 points, three ahead of St. Louis and Dallas.

Jonathan Bamba opened the scoring in the ninth minute for his first goal since March 21. The Fire's designated player dribbled to the top of the 18-yard box and bent a shot past goalkeeper Yohei Takaoka.

Zinckernagel finished a nice give-and-go with Haile-Selassie to make it 2-0 in the 50th. Zinckernagel's first goal since May came after he missed a penalty kick in the first half.

Vancouver defender Mathías Laborda scored in the 73rd by heading in Oliver Larraz's corner kick.

Vancouver, who will be getting some key players back from international duty, plays LAFC on the road Saturday, while Chicago hosts New York City FC on the same.

stories.headline: Basketball Power Index: NBA projections, playoff chances for 2026-27 season
stories.summary: ESPN's Basketball Power Index projections for the 2026-27 NBA season are out, including a ranking of all 30 teams.
stories.body:
The NBA season starts Tuesday, Oct. 20, and ESPN has multiple previews to guide readers, including a ranking of the top 100 players, a look at the top players in new places and capsules on each team, with the most important stats that affect teams' win-loss records.

Now it's time for a season preview using ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI), which evaluates two different strength measures for all 30 NBA teams: one based on players currently available, and the other based on players who should be available during the playoffs. Then, to create preseason projections, the BPI takes into account win totals from the betting market in conjunction with each team's schedule and other factors, simulating the season thousands of times, with the results forming these projections.

Once the season begins, the BPI watches what happens in games and updates both its current BPI and its playoff BPI. There are numerous benefits to this, particularly that it adjusts game predictions on the fly when there are reports of players missing games. If Giannis Antetokounmpo is going to miss a game, for instance, the BPI marks down the Miami Heat's chance to win that game by an amount suggested by history. Sometimes, those injury reports are late or inaccurate (ahem, Joel Embiid) and it annoys us, the BPI and the league as a whole. But don't hold that against the BPI's model.

One thing the BPI isn't seeing this season is a secret prediction edge over Las Vegas. There aren't major deviations in this model's rankings from what Vegas is forecasting.

Let's dig into the projections, including how it ranks teams from 1 to 30 and which teams have the best chance to win the NBA Finals.

Jump to a section:

1-30 team rankings

NBA playoff projections

NBA Finals projections

More takeaways

Regular-season projections

The BPI values shown are the current numbers, not the version for the playoffs. The Golden State Warriors are down at No. 20, reflecting the absence of Jimmy Butler III, who tore his ACL in January and could return around midseason. The Warriors would be No. 12 if they were at full strength.

There is only one other team with an injury causing significant deviations between their current and playoff power: Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers. That's because we know from history Embiid is going to miss games -- he has played 41 games per season since he was drafted and has played just 96 over the past three seasons -- and he is a good enough player that it matters. With Embiid, the Sixers have the third-best playoff BPI, consistent with the expectation they are among the favorites to come out of the East.

There are a few things to note from the overall league rankings. First, the Denver Nuggets finished last season as the league's best offense in the league, and the BPI isn't going to argue that they got worse. They've been in the top six on offense for seven years now. They're, of course, led by Nikola Jokic, who was the No. 1-ranked player in our top 100.

Second, the Oklahoma City Thunder are far and away the best-ranked defense at plus-5.7 to the second-place San Antonio Spurs at plus-4.2. The Thunder have been No. 1 on that side of the ball the past two seasons and just missed at No. 2 the season before.

Third, notice that the best teams are driven by defense (Thunder, Spurs, Detroit Pistons) and the worst teams are, well, likely driving their coaches wild with bad defense (Sacramento Kings, Milwaukee Bucks, New Orleans Pelicans). In most years, offense drives the greatest difference across teams, but not this season. The range between the best and worst offenses is 8.0 net points per game, but it's 10.4 on defense. This is merely a forecast and not a fact, but it's something to watch as the game continues to evolve.

NBA playoff projections

The BPI can occasionally be a little overconfident. The model believes six teams in the West have an 85% chance to make the playoffs. Those numbers imply that it's unlikely that even one of those slips out of the playoffs. I have my doubts.

That doubt comes from knowing there is a realistic chance that someone on those top six teams gets hurt and it matters. Maybe that's Jokic or Kevin Durant or Luka Doncic. Those stars are important, having all been in the top 10 in overall Net Points added last season. Plus, those teams don't have the bench of the Thunder, whose bench could have gotten a No. 7 or 8 seed by itself based on a reasonable interpretation of their talent. They seem more fragile than a 10% chance of missing the playoffs.

On the Eastern side of the ledger, the story isn't all that different, though the bottom few teams are a little messier. From No. 6 to No. 10, there is plenty of room for teams to make it or fall out of the playoffs, where the Charlotte Hornets and Washington Wizards are not even shown because we stopped at 10 teams.

Not mentioned in these season projections: The Boston Celtics have a 75% chance of having at least the same record as the rival Sixers. But, if they are to meet in the playoffs, that is where the healthy Embiid factor kicks in and the Sixers have a 52% chance to beat the Celtics in a series.

NBA Finals projections

The Thunder have about a 1 chance in 4 to win the title, per the BPI's projections. Here are some game scenarios about equal to a 25% chance to win, to give that a little perspective:

Being behind by eight points at halftime
Trailing by four points with about five minutes left to go
Down 2 with a minute to go, but without possession

These are exciting situations. No one is leaving the game then unless they were only there to watch a mascot make a reverse half-court shot. Having a 28% chance doesn't sound like much, but it is an interesting number. It makes the rest of the league feel like they have a good chance, but those Thunder fans are also feeling good.

The Sixers' 8% chance needs perspective, too. That 8% doesn't change much if they rise to the No. 1 seed, where they'd go up to about 12%, or if they drop to the No. 6 seed, where it remains about 8%. Because the East looks fairly even across the playoff teams, the depth of the Sixers' stars keeps them competitive in the playoffs (especially if Embiid is healthy), no matter which teams they play. But even Embiid doesn't significantly bring up their chances to win it all when the Thunder and Spurs are so strong.

More takeaways from ESPN's BPI projections
This is the first season of the new anti-tanking rules. The updated draft lottery format means that really bad teams actually have a lower chance to get the No. 1 pick compared to merely ordinary bad teams. We put the new lottery rules into the BPI's system and let it project what expected picks teams would get. The big news out of that is -- and this is a little depressing for fans of competitive balance -- the Thunder have the third-best odds of getting the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. Fortunately, it's only at about 11%, but they have about a 75% chance of getting a top-10 pick.

ESPN Analytics built this cool simulation of the lottery if you like watching balls bounce around to determine the fate of a franchise. I did it once just as I was writing the previous paragraph and it landed the Thunder the No. 3 pick. I had to remind myself this was just a simulation and not reality.

In general, the odds of landing the No. 1 pick are much more flat, due to the new rules and the forecast of how teams will do this season. The Kings, for example, are projected to be the worst team in the league and their chances to get the top pick are about 7%, which ranks seventh. The Dallas Mavericks are predicted to win 10 more games than the Kings and have an 8% chance at the No. 1 pick. The new lottery rules create incentive to pay attention in real time during the season to where teams are likely to end up.

Finally, just for fun, the BPI can predict the likelihood of winning and losing streaks. Two teams are at about 70% to have at least a 10-game winning streak -- the usual suspects in the Thunder and Spurs. Both had streaks that long last season, but so did the Pistons, Nuggets and Atlanta Hawks. Last season, though, was when tanking teams were happy to fall into someone else's winning streak. Three teams had 16-game losing streaks and that lack of competitiveness probably raised the number of double-digit win streaks, too.

Of course, the most surprising streak of the season was that of the New York Knicks, who won 13 straight in the playoffs. Beating good teams over and over again in a march to a title is a dream, a statistical marvel. As much as we'd like to believe in the data and the calculations of the BPI, the basketball season that is about to start has a lot of the human factor and reason to watch beyond the highlights. You don't need the predictions. Enjoy the ups and downs of a game. The BPI didn't need to predict ups and downs because they will happen. Doncic, Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jayson Tatum, LeBron James and many other stars will have amazing games. You don't have to predict them but watch them when you can.

Roll out the basketballs and let's play.

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.
stories.body:
Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.

It will also be the sixth and final sprint race of the season as Singapore hosts it for the first time.

Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the title championship to 84 points from George Russell.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 17th round of the season.

- Bahrain GP was the worst indictment of F1's new engine regs yet

- Could Malaysia return to F1 calendar? The state of play despite Sepang travel chaos

- Max Verstappen wins disrupted Bahrain GP, Kimi Antonelli extends title lead as George Russell retires

Singapore Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 9

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Sprint Qualifying: 1.30 p.m. - 2.14 p.m.

Saturday, October 10

Sprint: 10 a.m. - 11 a.m.

Qualifying: 2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Sunday, October 11

Singapore Grand Prix: 1 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Singapore Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Marina Bay Street Circuit

Singapore is one of the toughest challenges on the calendar for drivers due to the intense humidity and physically demanding nature of the circuit.

But this time round the drivers will have had a chance to get used to the humid conditions after racing in Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix last weekend.

The Marina Bay Circuit has been on the calendar since 2008 and is one of the standout tracks. The race takes place at night with its breathtaking views of the city's skyline as cars make their way through the tight and twisty circuit.

Drivers can lose around 3kg in body weight after each race due to the amount they sweat.

Singapore Grand Prix

Circuit: Marina Bay Street Circuit; Singapore

Previous winners in Singapore

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2022: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2023: Carlos Sainz (Ferrari)

2024: Lando Norris (McLaren)

2025: George Russell (Mercedes)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2008

Lap record: 1:33.808 Lewis Hamilton (2025)

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel has the most wins with five (2011-2013, 2015 and 2019). From the current grid, Hamilton has four wins (2009, 2014, 2017-2018) and Fernando Alonso with two (2008 and 2010). Pérez (2022), Sainz (2023), Norris (2024) and Russell (2025) have all won a race each here.

Most poles: Vettel (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017) and Hamilton (2009, 2012, 2014, 2018) share the pole record with four each. From the current grid, Charles Leclerc (2019, 2022) has had two pole positions here.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Singapore Grand Prix is set to be thundery showers and light winds throughout the weekend, with highs of 34°C on Friday. The temperature is forecast to drop a degree for the remainder of the weekend.

What happened last time out?
Russell claimed pole position in Singapore last year and crossed the line 0.182 seconds clear of Red Bull's Verstappen, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri behind.

Russell took his second win of the season, but there was plenty of other drama during the race, especially at McLaren.

Norris, who started in fifth, knocked into Piastri when trying to pass him in the first corner. Piastri managed to gain some ground towards the end of the race, but he had to settle for fourth on the day McLaren lifted the trophy for the constructors' title.

Piastri's drivers' championship lead to Norris was separated by only 22 points with six races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

One to watch this weekend is Red Bull and Verstappen after he won the race last weekend. The team brought major upgrades two races ago and improvements to its overall performance has been evident.

Russell, who suffered a major blow to his championship hopes after retiring last time out, will be looking to maximise the points on offer across the weekend.

Mercedes are expected to be strong, while Ferrari are quick in cornering speed. Hamilton has won four times here, so could be a threat. McLaren's Norris and Piastri fell under the radar and struggled for pace in Malaysia.

All will be to play for under the lights in Singapore as we head into the business end of the season.
